_readme: CodeBuddy Code's stream-json vocabulary (`codebuddy -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json`), for the tables that BOTH the Go provider and the TS renderer plugin read. CodeBuddy's stream is deliberately Claude Code 2.1.220-shaped, but the shapes LeapMux parses differ where it matters, so this contract shares no table with claude-protocol.json. `frameKinds` are the top-level `type` values on stdout. `controlRequestSubtypes` are the request subtypes LeapMux sends and the CLI sends back; both sides dispatch on them. `modes` are the four permission modes get_available_modes advertises. `effortLevels` are the --effort values CodeBuddy owns (not Claude's low/medium/high/ultra set). `systemSubtypes` are the system-line subtypes both sides classify. The can_use_tool answer fields (`allowed`, `reason`, `interrupt`, `updatedInput`) are Go-only: the browser sends the neutral behavior envelope and the worker alone translates it, so they live in providers/codebuddy/protocol.go, per the contracts rule's one-side-only exemption.
